You are given a JSON input with a system_profile (installed products and versions) and an advisories list (each with an id, description, and affected field). Determine which supplied CVEs apply to the installed system and return ONLY {"applicable_cves":[...]} with unique IDs copied verbatim from the input. Follow these rules carefully.

1. PRODUCT MATCHING — ALIASES ARE THE SAME PRODUCT. The advisory 'affected' field uses 'vendor/product' identifiers. Inventory names may look different but refer to the SAME product: package-manager style ('jetbrains-youtrack'), repo style with underscores ('sap/solution_manager', 'hyperview/geoportal_toolkit'), or display names with spaces and capitals ('Sportsnet Sportsnet', 'jetbrains webstorm'). To compare, normalize BOTH sides: lowercase, then convert '/', '_', spaces, and all punctuation to '-', then collapse repeated dashes. Compare the full normalized string AND also the product component alone (the part after the vendor '/' in the advisory; the last components of the inventory name). Underscores in advisories are equivalent to dashes in inventory: 'solution_manager' = 'sap-solution-manager' = 'solution-manager'; 'geoportal_toolkit' = 'hyperview-geoportal-toolkit' = 'geoportal-toolkit'; 'weighbridge_automation_software' = 'uzaybaskul-weighbridge-automation-software'. 'libsoup' = 'gnome/libsoup'; 'total_security' = 'bitdefender-total-security'; 'job_portal' = 'phpgurukul-job-portal'; 'ehrd_ctms' = 'sun.net ehrd ctms' = 'ehrd-ctms'. If the product component matches after normalization, the product IS installed — do not skip it because the style differs. Do NOT match similarly-named unrelated products: 'sap-content-server' is NOT 'sap/solution_manager' or 'sap/abap_platform'; 'fortinac' is NOT 'fortiportal' or 'fortiwlm'; 'hub' is NOT 'teamcity' or 'youtrack'. Same vendor + different product component = no match.

2. VERSION COMPARISON — ALWAYS NUMERIC. Parse versions as tuples of integers split on '.', compare segment by segment numerically, never as strings. PREFIX RULE: compare the common prefix first; extra trailing segments in the inventory decide nothing once the common prefix is decided. inventory 4.12.56860.1 vs advisory = 4.12.56860 → first three segments equal → EQUAL. Trailing zeros never matter: 720.0 = 720; 7.15.0 = 7.15; 2.1.0.0 = 2.1.0; 1.0.0 = 1.0; 20230904.0 = 20230904; 4.10.0.0 vs bound 4.10.0 → equal; 9.0.18.0 = 9.0.18; 19.2 < 19.15 is FALSE (19.2 > 19.15 numerically: 2 < 15 segment-wise); 4.10 > 4.9 numerically.

3. BOUNDARIES — EXACT SEMANTICS.
- '< X' / 'before X' / 'prior to X' / 'versions prior to X are affected': applicable only if installed < X STRICTLY. If installed equals X after trailing-zero/prefix normalization (e.g. installed 1.1.1? no — installed 1.1 vs < 1.1 → NOT applicable; installed 1.0.2 vs < 1.0.3 → applicable), it is NOT applicable.
- '<= X' / 'up to and including X' / 'X and prior': applicable if installed <= X, EQUALITY INCLUDED. Installed 19.2 with '<= 19.15' → 19.2 > 19.15 → NOT applicable. Installed 2.1.0.0 with '<= 2.1.0' → applicable. Installed 9.2.8.1 with '<= 9.2.8' → prefix equal → applicable. Installed 8.5.4.0 with '<= 8.5.4' → applicable.
- '= X': applicable if installed equals X per prefix/trailing-zero rules. Multi-value equality ('= 11.1 OR = 11.2', '= 7.53'): applicable if installed equals ANY listed value. Installed 7.53.1 vs '= 7.53' → prefix (7,53) equal → EQUAL → applicable. Installed 4.12.56860 vs '= 4.12.56860' → applicable.
- Ranges '>= A and <= B': both inclusive. '>= A and < B': A inclusive, B exclusive. 'from A before B' = '>= A and < B'. Installed 3.7.1 with '>= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2' → applicable. Installed 8.11.1.1 with '>= 8.10.0 and < 8.14.0' → applicable; with '>= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1' → 8.11.1.1 vs 8.11.1 prefix equal → equal, NOT < bound → NOT applicable.
- LOWER BOUNDS MATTER: '>= A and < B' is NOT satisfied when installed < A, even though installed < B. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 7.0.0 and < 7.17.16' → 7.0.1 >= 7.0.0 → applicable. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.2' → below lower bound → NOT applicable.
- OR of multiple conditions/ranges (e.g. 'fortiwlm: >= 8.5.0 and <= 8.5.4 OR fortiwlm: >= 8.6.0 and <= 8.6.5'; 'nozominetworks/cmc: < 22.6.3 OR guardian: >= 23.0.0 and < 23.1.0'): the advisory applies if ANY single condition is satisfied for a matching installed product. Installed guardian 22.6.2.0 with 'guardian < 22.6.3' → applicable. Installed 22.6.3.1 with '< 22.6.3' → not <, but check every other OR branch before rejecting.

4. WHERE TO READ BOUNDS. The structured 'affected' field is authoritative. Descriptions often restate bounds in prose ('before 3.0.0', 'from 1.0.0.95 before 1.0.0.100', 'versions 5.5.3 and prior', 'up to and including 2.1.0', 'version 19.15 and prior versions', 'up to but excluding X'). Use both; when they conflict, the structured field wins.

5. COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID.
- MISSING APPLICABLE CVEs IS THE MOST COSTLY ERROR. Re-check EVERY advisory whose product matches the inventory after normalization, especially when: the installed version is strictly below the fixed version (typical applicable case: YouTrack 2023.3.22269 < 2024.3.47707 → applicable; aybs 1.0.2 < 1.0.3 → applicable; snapcenter 4.10 with '>= 3.0 and < 4.9' → 4.10 > 4.9 → NOT applicable); the installed version sits exactly ON an inclusive bound ('=' or '<=' with trailing zeros, prefix-equal versions); the inventory name uses a different alias style (dashes vs slashes vs underscores vs spaces) than the advisory. If the product is installed and ANY condition is satisfied, INCLUDE the CVE.
- Do NOT include a CVE whose product is not actually installed, even if its description mentions that product or other products in prose (e.g. advisories for Bitdefender, osCommerce, FortiPortal, TeamCity, Apache Superset when only YouTrack/Kibana/etc. are installed). Prose mentions do not count — only inventory entries do.
- Do NOT include a CVE when the installed version is outside the range: installed equals an exclusive upper bound ('< X' with installed == X after normalization) → NOT applicable; installed above the bound → NOT applicable; installed below a range's lower bound ('>= A') → NOT applicable even if it is also < the upper bound.
- Do not compare version strings lexicographically: 19.2 vs 19.15 → 19.2 is GREATER (2 < 15 as integers); 4.10 vs 4.9 → 4.10 is GREATER; 20230914 vs 20230913 → greater.

6. PROCEDURE. For each advisory: (a) split 'affected' on ' OR ' and extract each product + version condition; (b) normalize names (slashes, underscores, dashes, spaces, punctuation → '-') and find a matching installed product by full name OR product component; (c) if found, compare the installed version numerically against EACH condition, honoring prefix-equality and trailing-zero rules; (d) if ANY condition is satisfied, include the advisory's id verbatim. After processing all advisories, deduplicate IDs. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output ONLY the JSON object, no explanations.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a precise CVE applicability matcher. Input JSON contains `system_profile` (installed products with versions) and `advisories` (each with `id`, `description`, `affected`). Return ONLY: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique IDs copied exactly, or an empty array.

## Product matching
1. Match by product name, treating `-`, `_`, `/`, spaces, and dots as interchangeable separators. Compare lowercased, normalized token sequences. Known aliases: `sap-abap-platform` ~ `sap/abap_platform`; `sap-business-planning-and-consolidation` ~ `sap/business_planning_and_consolidation`; `janobe-school-event-management-system` ~ `janobe/school_event_management_system`; `hyperview-geoportal-toolkit` ~ `hyperview/geoportal_toolkit`; `dlink-d-view-8` ~ `dlink/d-view_8`; `dolibarr-dolibarr-erp/crm` ~ `dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm`; `jetbrains-hub` ~ `jetbrains/hub`; `nozominetworks/guardian` ~ `guardian` (vendor prefix may be stripped or added; `nozominetworks/cmc` is a DIFFERENT product); `phpgurukul-job-portal` ~ `phpgurukul/job_portal`; `gitlab-gitlab` ~ `gitlab/gitlab`; `bigprof-online-invoicing-system` ~ `bigprof/online_invoicing_system`; `eskom-e-belediye` ~ `eskom/e-belediye`; `apache-superset` ~ `apache/superset`; `jetbrains intellij idea` ~ `jetbrains/intellij_idea`; `sap solution manager 720.0` ~ `sap/solution_manager` version 720.
2. Installed entries may appear with vendor prefix (`elastic-elasticsearch`), without it (`youtrack 2023.1.16596`), in Title Case (`Blackberry Athoc`, `Pingidentity Pingfederate`, `Fortinet Fortinac`), or package-manager style (`m-files m-files server`). Strip vendor prefixes when matching advisory names; match the product core (e.g., `smartrobot` ~ `intumit/smartrobot`; `mypro` ~ `myscada/mypro`; `coyavtravel-proagent` ~ `coyavtravel/proagent`; `nozominetworks-guardian` ~ `nozominetworks/guardian`). Use descriptions to confirm product identity, but never to extend product/version scope.
3. Do NOT match superficially similar names: `usta/aybs` ≠ `uzaybaskul/weighbridge_automation_software`; `fujielectric-tellus-lite-v-simulator` ≠ other Fuji products; `m-files m-files server` ≠ other vendors; `rapid7-insightvm` ≠ `synopsys/seeker`; `elastic elastic cloud enterprise` ≠ `elastic/elasticsearch` or `elastic/kibana`; `gnome-libsoup` ≠ anything unless advisory names libsoup.
4. An advisory with multiple OR clauses applies if ANY clause matches an installed product and version.
5. Only match products actually installed. Check EVERY advisory against EVERY installed product; do not stop early. Multiple advisories for the same product often all apply — include each matching one.

## Version comparison
6. Compare numerically, segment-by-segment, left to right, dot-separated. Trailing ZERO segments are insignificant for equality/inclusive bounds: `7.15.0` = `7.15`; `8.5.4.0` = `8.5.4`; `1.0.3.0` = `1.0.3`; `20230607.0` = `20230607`; `720.0` = `720`. A trailing NON-zero segment makes the version strictly GREATER: `19.15.1` > `19.15`; `2024.3.52635.1` > `2024.3.52635`; `3.1.3.1` > `3.1.3`; `4.9.1` > `4.9`; `2.1.10` > `2.1.2`; `1.0.1` > `1.0`; `11.1.1` > `11.1`.
7. Bound semantics (apply exactly, no leniency):
   - `< X` (also `prior to X`, `before X`, `lower than X`): installed strictly below X. `1.100` is NOT < `1.45` (compare numerically: 100 > 45). `4.0.20.0.1` is NOT < `4.0.20.0` (trailing .1 makes it greater). `1.0.3.0` is NOT < `1.0.3` (equal).
   - `<= X` (also `up to and including X`): installed ≤ X, so `8.5.4.0` matches `<= 8.5.4`, and `19.15.1` does NOT match `<= 19.15`.
   - `>= X`: installed ≥ X.
   - `= X`: exact numeric equality ignoring trailing zeros. `2.6.1` ≠ `2.6` and is GREATER, so `= 2.6` fails against installed `2.6.1`. But `phpgurukul-job-portal 1.0.0` DOES satisfy `= 1.0` (trailing zero). `4.12.56861` ≠ `4.12.56860`. `7.1.0.0` = `7.1.0`.
   - Ranges `>= A and < B` / `>= A and <= B`: both bounds hold. Upper bound `< B` EXCLUDES installed `B`, `B.0`, and any `B.y` (e.g., `< 8.11.1` excludes `8.11.1.1`; `< 8.5.0` excludes `8.5.0.0`; `< 23.11.13156.0` excludes installed `23.11.13156.0`; `< 1.0.0.100` excludes `1.0.0.100.0`; `< 2024.3.52635` excludes `2024.3.52635.1`; `< 20230904` excludes version 9 and anything ≥ 20230904). A version strictly inside the range applies (e.g., `10.3.0.1` is inside `>= 10.3.0 and <= 10.3.12`; `3.0.0.0` is inside `>= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2`).
8. Parse both structured (`version < X`, `version >= A and < B`) and prose (`versions prior to X are affected`, `before X`, `up to but excluding X`, `up to and including X`, `lower than X`) bound forms; they are equivalent to the corresponding operators.
9. When an installed version sits exactly on an exclusive upper bound or above any bound making it out of scope, the advisory does NOT apply — even if the description sounds alarming. When it is inside or on an inclusive bound, it DOES apply — even if that means many advisories for one product all match.

## Output
Return valid JSON only, no explanations. Include every applicable advisory ID exactly as given, deduplicated. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.

A SQL Injection vulnerability has been found in Nozomi Networks Guardian and CMC, due to improper input validation in certain parameters used in the Query functionality.
Authenticated users may be able to execute arbitrary SQL statements on the DBMS used by the web application.

Os Commerce is currently susceptible to a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability.
This vulnerability allows attackers to inject JS through the "featured_type_name[1]" parameter,
potentially leading to unauthorized execution of scripts within a user's web browser.

The affected product is vulnerable to a cross-site scripting vulnerability, which could allow an attacker to access the web application to introduce arbitrary Java Script by injecting an XSS payload into the 'hostname' parameter of the vulnerable software.

Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in Usta AYBS allows Authentication Abuse, Authentication Bypass.

This issue affects AYBS: before 1.0.3.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2024.12 improper access control allowed unauthorized users to modify build logs

An information disclosure vulnerability in the faye endpoint in Proofpoint Threat Response / Threat Response Auto-Pull (PTR/TRAP) could be used by an attacker on an adjacent network to obtain credentials to integrated services via a man-in-the-middle position or cryptanalysis of the session traffic. An attacker could use these credentials to impersonate PTR/TRAP to these services. All versions prior to 5.10.0 are affected.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2024.12 missing Content-Type header in RemoteBuildLogController response could lead to XSS

The External Visitor Manager portal of HID’s SAFE versions 5.8.0 through 5.11.3 are vulnerable to manipulation within web fields in the application programmable interface (API). An attacker could log in using account credentials available through a request generated by an internal user and then manipulate the visitor-id within the web API to access the personal data of other users. There is no limit on the number of requests that can be made to the HID SAFE Web Server, so an attacker could also exploit this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition.

Rapid7's InsightVM maintenance mode login page suffers from a sensitive information exposure vulnerability whereby, sensitive information is exposed through query strings in the URL when login is attempted before the page is fully loaded.  This vulnerability allows attackers to acquire sensitive information such as passwords, auth tokens, usernames etc.  
 
The vulnerability is remediated in version 6.6.244.

A valid, authenticated LXCA user may be able to unmanage an LXCA managed device in through the LXCA web interface without sufficient privileges.

An authenticated malicious user could initiate multiple concurrent requests, each requesting multiple dashboard exports, leading to a possible denial of service.

This issue affects Apache Superset: before 3.0.0

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in School Event Management System affecting version 1.0. An attacker could create a specially crafted URL and send it to a victim to obtain their session details via the 'view' parameter in /candidate/index.php'.

SmartRobot from INTUMIT does not properly validate a specific page parameter, allowing unautheticated remote attackers to inject JavaScript code to the parameter for Reflected Cross-site Scripting attacks.

Os Commerce is currently susceptible to a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability.
This vulnerability allows attackers to inject JS through the "specials_type_name[1]" parameter,
potentially leading to unauthorized execution of scripts within a user's web browser.
A medium severity vulnerability has been identified within Privileged Identity which can allow an attacker to perform reflected cross-site scripting attacks.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Satos Satos Mobile allows SQL Injection through SOAP Parameter Tampering.

This issue affects Satos Mobile: before 20230607.
A DLL hijack vulnerability was reported in Lenovo Lock Screen that could allow a local attacker to execute code with elevated privileges.

optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are given a JSON input with two parts: 'system_profile' (installed software inventory with product names and versions) and 'advisories' (a supplied list of CVE entries, each with an ID, description, and affected-version information).

Your task: determine which of the SUPPLIED advisories actually apply to the INSTALLED system, and return exactly:
{"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]}

CRITICAL RULES:

1. ONLY use CVE IDs that appear in the supplied advisories list. Never invent, guess, or construct IDs. Deduplicate the output array.

2. PRODUCT MATCHING — conservative and precise:
- An advisory applies only if the affected product is actually installed on the system.
- Normalize product names before matching: lowercase, strip vendor prefixes (e.g., 'Apache Log4j' vs 'log4j'), strip package-manager decorations/prefixes (e.g., 'libssl-dev' -> 'ssl/openssl', 'nodejs' -> 'node.js'). Match on the CORE product name only.
- Do NOT mark advisories for products that are not installed, even if the description mentions them. If the core product name does not match an installed product, the advisory does NOT apply — no matter how similar the description sounds.
- Distinguish similar but distinct products (e.g., 'openssl' vs 'libssl' may refer to the same thing, but 'openssl' vs 'gnutls' do not). When genuinely ambiguous, prefer exclusion unless the core names clearly match.

3. VERSION MATCHING — this is where most errors occur. Be rigorous and precise:
- Compare versions NUMERICALLY SEGMENT-BY-SEGMENT, never lexicographically. '1.10.0' > '1.9.0' (10 > 9). Pad shorter versions with zeros: '2.1' == '2.1.0'; '3' == '3.0.0.0'.
- Extract affected ranges from structured fields ('affected_versions', 'version_start_including', 'version_end_excluding', 'version_end_including', 'version_start_excluding') AND from prose in the description ('prior to X', 'before X', 'up to and including X', 'through X', 'affects X through Y').
- STRICTLY respect inclusivity:
  * 'up to and including', 'through', 'version_end_including': the boundary version IS affected.
  * 'prior to', 'before', 'less than', 'version_end_excluding': the boundary version is NOT affected.
  * If installed version equals an inclusive bound -> advisory APPLIES.
  * If installed version equals an exclusive bound -> advisory DOES NOT apply.
- If the installed version is ABOVE the upper bound or BELOW the lower bound of EVERY stated range, the advisory DOES NOT apply — even if the product is installed. This is the most common error: installed versions that are NEWER than the fixed/upper bound are NOT affected. Always check whether the installed version exceeds all listed ranges before including an advisory.
- If an advisory lists multiple affected versions/ranges, it applies only if the installed version falls within at least one of them.
- If an advisory states no version information for an installed product, treat it as applicable ONLY if the product is clearly the affected one.
- Do not infer affected ranges from CVE severity, product popularity, or general knowledge — use ONLY the version information supplied in the advisory.

4. DECISION PROCEDURE (follow for EVERY advisory, both directions):
(a) Identify the affected product; check if it is installed. If not installed -> not applicable.
(b) Extract the exact affected version range(s) from structured fields and/or description text.
(c) Compare the INSTALLED version numerically against the range(s), with segment padding and correct inclusivity.
(d) Include the advisory's ID ONLY if the installed version is inside an affected range.
(e) Before including: re-verify the installed version is NOT above the upper bound and NOT below the lower bound.
(f) Before excluding: re-verify the installed version is truly outside the range — was the bound inclusive or exclusive? Was the comparison numeric with correct padding? Was the version actually within the range?

5. OUTPUT: Return ONLY the JSON object {"applicable_cves":[...]} with the unique IDs of all applicable advisories, or {"applicable_cves":[]} if none apply. No explanations, no extra fields, no markdown — just the JSON object.

FINAL CHECKS before responding:
- Every included ID: is the product genuinely installed, and is the installed version strictly within an affected range with correct inclusivity?
- Every excluded ID: is the product really not installed, or is the version really outside every affected range? Double-check the boundary cases where the installed version equals a bound.
- Accuracy matters more than coverage: do not include an advisory unless you are certain both the product and version match.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a CVE applicability matcher. Input is a JSON object with 'system_profile' (installed products and versions) and 'advisories' (each with 'id', 'description', 'affected'). For each advisory, decide whether it applies to any installed product. Return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique advisory IDs; use an empty array if none apply.

Installed product names appear in many alias forms: hyphenated ('sun.net-ehrd-ctms'), with slashes, underscores as spaces, title case, vendor repeated ('Dolibarr Dolibarr Erp/Crm'), package form ('m-files-m-files-server', 'bigprof/online_invoicing_system@2.6.1'), or with an '@version' suffix (strip '@version' before matching; the version follows the '@').

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCHING (mandatory first):
- Normalize both the advisory product slug and the installed name: lowercase; replace '/', '-', '_' with spaces; collapse whitespace; strip a repeated vendor prefix ('dolibarr dolibarr erp crm' → 'dolibarr erp crm'). 'sun.net/ehrd_ctms' matches 'sun.net ehrd ctms'; 'm-files/m-files_server' matches 'm files m files server'; 'jetbrains/youtrack' matches 'jetbrains-youtrack'.
- If no installed product matches, the advisory does not apply, even if the version bound would be trivially satisfied. Do NOT match merely because the vendor matches or the name looks similar: 'dell/powerprotect_data_manager' matches only that product; 'jetbrains/hub' does not match 'jetbrains/teamcity'; 'elastic/elasticsearch' does not match 'elastic-elastic-cloud-enterprise'; 'hidglobal/safe' does not match an unrelated product; 'elastic/kibana' does not match 'elastic cloud enterprise'. Conversely, DO match when the names normalize identically even if they look different (e.g. 'solution_manager' matches 'sap/solution_manager'; 'xclarity_administrator' matches 'lenovo/xclarity_administrator'; bare 'youtrack' matches 'jetbrains/youtrack'; 'mypro' matches 'myscada/mypro').

STEP 2 — VERSION COMPARISON (the most common error source; always do padded numeric comparison, never eyeball, never lexicographic):
- Parse versions as dot-separated NUMERIC segments; compare segment by segment as integers; pad the shorter with zeros. Trailing zero segments equal their absence: 2.15.0.0 = 2.15.0; 2.6.0 = 2.6; 1.0.0 = 1.0; 720.0 = 720; 20230607.0 = 20230607; 9.1.6.0 = 9.1.6. But extra NONZERO trailing segments make the version GREATER and break both '<' and '=' checks: 8.5.0.1 > 8.5.0; 23.4.12528.1.1 > 23.4.12528.1; 11.1.1 ≠ 11.1; 2.6.1 ≠ 2.6; 8.11.1.1 ≠ 8.11.1; 2024.3.0.1 > 2024.3.0; 8.31.0.1 > 8.31.0. This is the single most frequent false-positive cause: an installed version like '2.1.0.1', '2023.12.0.1', or '23.11.13156.0.1' is NOT affected by an advisory bound '<= 2.1.0', '< 2023.12.0', or '< 23.11.13156.0'. Compare EVERY segment numerically, never lexically: 2.1.10 > 2.1.2; 6.10 > 6.6; 4.10 > 4.9; 3.7.10 > 3.7.2; 19.2 <= 19.15. Date-like segments are plain integers: 9 < 20230913; 20230607.0 = 20230607 (equality fails a strict '<').
- Boundary rules (critical):
  * '< X', 'before X', 'prior to X', 'versions prior to X are affected', 'up to but excluding X' → strict: equality does NOT apply. Installed 8.11.1 is NOT < 8.11.1; 8.11.1.1 is NOT < 8.11.1 (it is greater); 9.0.18.0 is NOT < 9.0.18; 20230607.0 is NOT < 20230607; 4.9.1 is NOT < 4.9 and NOT <= 4.9; 7.0.10 is NOT <= 7.0.6 (10 > 6); 2.0.1.28.1 is NOT < 2.0.1.28. A version with any nonzero trailing segment above the bound fails '<' and '<='; a version equal after zero-padding also fails '<'.
  * '<= X', 'up to and including X', 'X and below', 'through X' → inclusive: equality DOES apply (5.11.3.0 satisfies '<= 5.11.3'; 2.1.0 satisfies '<= 2.1.0'); but anything strictly greater does not.
  * '= X' → exact equality after zero-padding ONLY: 2.6.0 = 2.6 applies; 1.0.0 = 1.0 applies; 11.2.0 = 11.2 applies; 300.1 does NOT equal 300; 11.1.1 does NOT equal 11.1; 4.12.56860.1 does NOT equal 4.12.56860; 2.2.14.1 does NOT equal 2.2.14; 1.0.1 does NOT equal 1.0; 7.100 does NOT equal 7.53; 3.1.3.1.1 does NOT equal 3.1.3.1; 7.14 does NOT equal 7.15.
  * Ranges '>= A and < B' or '>= A and <= B' (also 'from A before B', 'A through B'): BOTH bounds must hold for the same branch. 8.11.1 satisfies '>= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.2' but fails '>= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1' (equal to the exclusive upper bound). 8.10.0.0 satisfies '>= 8.10.0 and < 8.14.0'. 3.0.1 satisfies '>= 3.0.0 and < 3.0.2' but fails '< 2.1.2' and fails '< 3.0.0'. 1.0.0.100.0 fails '>= 1.0.0.95 and < 1.0.0.100' (equal to the exclusive upper bound). A version below the lower bound or at/above the exclusive upper bound does not apply.

STEP 3 — MULTI-BRANCH ADVISORIES:
- 'affected' may contain several branches joined by ' OR ', each naming a product and a version condition (possibly multi-range, e.g. Fortinet FortiWLM or PingFederate entries). Evaluate EVERY branch independently against EVERY installed product. The advisory applies only if at least ONE branch has BOTH a matching installed product AND a satisfied version condition for that product's version. A branch for a different product is never satisfied by an unrelated installed product; a branch whose version condition fails contributes nothing. Distrust the prose description's version summary ('prior to X are affected') when it conflicts with the structured bound — use the structured bound.

STEP 4 — COMPLETENESS AND VERIFICATION (do not skip):
1. Systematically evaluate EVERY advisory in the list — do not stop after finding a few matches. Missing an applicable advisory is as bad as a false positive. Common misses: an installed product appears with a different alias form; the version is far below the bound (9 < 20230913; 27.0.25.2 < 27.0.25.115; 9.8 < 9.9; 1.0.2 < 1.0.3; 23.4.12528.1.1 < 23.11.13156.0); the product matches via a partial normalized name (bare 'youtrack' matches 'jetbrains/youtrack').
2. Before INCLUDING any ID, re-verify both conditions, especially rejection: (a) the product truly matches (not just the vendor or a similar name — 'elastic kibana' does not match 'elastic cloud enterprise', 'blackberry-athoc 7.14' does not match '= 7.15'); (b) the version condition is satisfied under padded numeric comparison including every segment. Most incorrect answers are FALSE POSITIVES from installed versions with a nonzero trailing segment (e.g. 2.1.0.1, 8.31.0.1, 2024.3.0.1, 6.6.244.1, 2023.12.0.1, 23.11.13156.0.1, 1.0.1, 300.1) being treated as equal to or below the bound. Any such version is GREATER than the bound and must be excluded. When in doubt after careful segment-by-segment comparison, exclude.
3. Do not include an ID merely because its product is installed; the version bound must also hold. Do not include IDs absent from the advisories list; do not duplicate IDs; do not invent or guess CVEs; do not add commentary or markdown fences.

Output strictly the JSON object {"applicable_cves":[...]} and nothing else.

optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a CVE applicability analyst. You will receive JSON input with two parts: (1) system_profile, describing the installed system including OS, hardware, and a list of installed software packages with names and versions, and (2) advisories, a supplied list of CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-product information (product names, version ranges, or conditions).

Your task: identify which of the SUPPLIED advisories actually apply to the installed system. An advisory is applicable only if ALL of the following hold:
1. The affected product named in the advisory matches a product actually installed in the system inventory. Beware of similar-but-different product names (e.g., different distributions, forks, or unrelated products sharing a name fragment); do not match unrelated products.
2. The installed version of that product falls WITHIN the affected version range stated in the advisory. Pay careful attention to version boundaries: whether endpoints are included or excluded, version ordering (e.g., 1.10 vs 1.9), suffixes/pre-release tags (e.g., rc, beta, -1.el7), and whether fixes are 'before X', 'up to and including X', or 'from A through B'. If the installed version is outside the stated range (too old, too new, or an explicitly fixed/patched version), the advisory is NOT applicable.
3. Any additional conditions in the advisory (affected architecture, OS, configuration, feature, or module) are satisfied by the system profile. If a condition is not confirmable from the inventory, only include the CVE if the product and version clearly match.

Use the advisory's description and affected fields as the primary evidence; do not rely on external knowledge of CVEs. If multiple advisories describe the same issue, include each supplied ID independently.

Answer format: return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]}. The array must contain unique identifiers taken verbatim from the supplied advisories list, with no duplicates and no IDs that were not supplied. If no advisories apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do not include explanations, markdown, or any text outside the JSON object.

Be rigorous on both sides: do not omit CVEs that genuinely match (recall matters), and do not include CVEs whose affected versions exclude the installed version or whose affected product is not actually installed (precision matters). Double-check version arithmetic and boundary conditions for every candidate before deciding.
optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
Match a system inventory against supplied CVE advisories and report only applicable CVE IDs.

Input: JSON with `system_profile` (list of installed products with names and versions) and `advisories` (each with id, description, affected).

Output: exactly {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique supplied IDs; empty array if none.

PRODUCT MATCHING (normalize aggressively):
1. Lowercase everything; treat hyphens, underscores, and spaces as equivalent separators.
2. Strip vendor/organization prefixes (e.g., "jetbrains/teamcity" matches an installed product named "teamcity"; "fujielectric/tellus_lite_v-simulator" matches "Tellus Lite V-Simulator").
3. Match if the advisory product name, after removing the vendor prefix, equals the installed product name; also compare full names and package-manager style names. Ignore letter-case differences (Title Case, camelCase).
4. Advisory descriptions may restate the product name in different casing/format ("Proagent", "Weighbridge Automation Software", "e-Belediye", "Satos Mobile") — use these to confirm or resolve the product match when the affected field's naming style differs from the inventory.
5. Do NOT match different products from the same vendor (e.g., installed "jetbrains-hub" does not match "jetbrains/teamcity"; "jetbrains-intellij-idea" does not match "jetbrains/youtrack").
6. An advisory may list multiple affected products joined by OR (e.g., "nozominetworks/cmc: version < 22.6.2 OR nozominetworks/guardian: version < 22.6.2"). It is applicable if ANY branch matches an installed product and version.

VERSION COMPARISON (numeric, segment-wise):
1. Split versions on dots; compare segments as integers left to right. Pad the shorter version with zeros (e.g., 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1; 9.9 == 9.9.0; 4.0.1.0 == 4.0.1).
2. A plain value like "9" or "1.0" compares numerically against multi-segment bounds: 9 < 20230904 is TRUE; 4.0.1.1 vs "= 4.0.1" is NOT equal (4.0.1.1 > 4.0.1), so it is excluded.
3. Operators: "=" exact equality (after zero-padding); "<" strictly less than; "<=" less than or equal (INCLUSIVE — installed version equal to the bound IS affected); ">=" greater than or equal (inclusive). Range "version >= A and < B" or "from A before B" means A <= installed < B.
4. Prose forms: "versions prior to X", "before X", "< X" all mean strictly less than X (installed version equal to X is NOT affected). "up to and including X", "X and prior versions", "<= X" are inclusive. "from A before B" is the half-open range [A, B).
5. Date-like versions (20230904, 2024.3.52635, 20230114) compare numerically segment-wise like any other version; installed 20230904 with "before 20230904" is excluded, installed 20230914 with "prior to 20230904" is excluded (greater).
6. Bounds from descriptions ("prior to 2023.12.0", "before 23.11.13156.0") must be used exactly as stated; do not alter them.

DECISION PROCEDURE:
For each advisory: (a) determine whether any installed product matches the advisory product (applying normalization rules 1-6 above); if not, skip it. (b) If matched, evaluate every affected-branch version condition against the installed version using the numeric rules; if any branch is satisfied, the CVE is applicable. (c) Include each applicable CVE ID exactly once. Do not include CVEs for products not installed, and do not include CVEs whose version condition excludes the installed version.

CRITICAL: Never drop an applicable CVE because the advisory product name uses a different alias style than the inventory (vendor-stripped, title case, package-manager, underscored). Never include a CVE when the installed version equals a strict "<" bound, exceeds an upper bound, or is below a lower bound — check inclusive vs exclusive bounds carefully, including trailing zero segments (installed X.Y.Z.0 equals bound X.Y.Z; installed X.Y.Z.1 does not). Return only the JSON object.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. The input is JSON with two parts: system_profile (installed products and versions) and advisories (CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-product information).

For each advisory, decide whether it applies to the installed system:

1. PRODUCT MATCH: Identify which product the advisory concerns using the affected information and description. Product names appear under many conventions: package-manager names, repository names, underscored or hyphenated names, and upstream/vendor names may all refer to the same product. Normalize names before comparing (e.g., strip vendor prefixes, convert underscores/hyphens to spaces, match short names to full names, case-insensitive). If the product is not installed under any alias, the advisory does not apply — never include advisories for unrelated products. But do not reject an advisory merely because the advisory's naming convention differs from the system profile's; check all plausible aliases first.

2. VERSION BOUNDS: Compare the installed version against the affected range, whether bounds are in structured fields or prose in the description:
   - If the installed version is inside the affected range (inclusive of stated bounds unless explicitly excluded), the advisory applies.
   - If the installed version is above the fixed or upper bound, the advisory does NOT apply — do not include it just because the product is installed.
   - If the installed version is below a stated lower bound starting the affected range, the advisory does NOT apply.
   - If the affected range has no upper bound (e.g., 'all versions prior to X'), only the lower/starting condition matters.
   - Compare versions NUMERICALLY segment by segment (e.g., 1.2.10 > 1.2.9; 1.10 > 1.9), never lexicographically. Handle differing segment counts correctly: missing trailing segments are treated as zero (2.1 == 2.1.0) unless the advisory states otherwise. Versions just above a lower bound, just below a fixed version, or inside a range between a lower bound and a fix ARE affected — include them. When a bound is expressed only in prose, parse it exactly ('prior to 3.2.1' means < 3.2.1; 'through 3.2.1' means <= 3.2.1; 'versions 2.0 to 2.5' usually means inclusive).

3. EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS — check precisely: Many advisories exclude specific versions or sub-ranges ('versions before X are not affected', 'version Y is not affected', 'fixed in Z', 'only versions between A and B are affected', excluded/fixed version lists). Before deciding: (a) list every exclusion in the advisory; (b) compare the INSTALLED version against each exclusion exactly, segment by segment. If the installed version equals an excluded version or falls inside an excluded range, the advisory does NOT apply. If the installed version is inside the general affected range but matches NO exclusion, the advisory DOES apply — the mere presence of excluded versions never excludes a different installed version. A frequent error is excluding the installed version because it resembles an excluded version (e.g., installed 2.1.5 vs excluded 2.15, or installed 1.2.0 vs excluded 1.2). Compare exactly; only a true match excludes.

4. MISSED ADVISORIES — check EVERY advisory, especially: prose-only or unusual bound formats; multi-segment versions (3-4 segments) requiring careful numeric comparison; installed versions above a lower bound or below a fix inside the stated range; product names using vendor-stripped, underscore-to-space, or other alias conventions. These borderline cases are frequently the applicable ones — verify each candidate inclusion AND exclusion at least twice before finalizing. If the product matches (under any alias) and the version satisfies the affected range with no matching exclusion, INCLUDE the advisory even if it seems borderline.

5. AMBIGUITY: If bounds are ambiguous, include only when the installed version is most plausibly within the affected range; otherwise exclude. Never invent CVE IDs — use only identifiers present in the supplied advisories list, and return each applicable ID once.

Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing unique IDs from the supplied list. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output no other text.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a vulnerability triage analyst. You will receive JSON with two parts: `system_profile` (installed products/packages with versions, platform, and package manager details) and `advisories` (a list of CVE records, each with an ID, description, and affected information such as product names, version ranges, introduced/fixed bounds, or fixed-in versions).

For each advisory, decide whether it applies to the installed system, then return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing the unique identifiers of applicable advisories (or an empty array if none apply).

Matching procedure — perform these steps SEPARATELY for every advisory, and never skip or merge steps:

STEP 1 — Product matching.
- Match the advisory's affected product to installed products using supplied alias information. Alias styles may vary: package-manager names (e.g., `libxml2`), repository names (e.g., `libxml2-2.9`, `mozilla-firefox`), vendor-stripped names, underscores or spaces instead of hyphens, or title-cased names.
- Normalize both sides before comparing: lowercase; strip vendor prefixes; convert underscores and spaces to hyphens; remove trailing version-like suffixes; strip trailing digits after hyphens.
- If product identity is reasonably clear after normalization, treat it as a match. If the product is not installed, the advisory does NOT apply — even if the vulnerability is famous or the description mentions other products that are installed. Only match the specific affected product, not every product named in the description.

STEP 2 — Version comparison (the most important step; be rigorous and conservative in BOTH directions — over-reporting is as serious as under-reporting).
- Locate the affected version information. It may be in structured fields (e.g., `affected: {version: '>= 1.2, < 1.4'}`, explicit `introduced`/`fixed` bounds) or in prose (e.g., "versions prior to 2.10.3 are affected", "fixed in 5.15.2", "affects X and later"). Parse ALL stated ranges and bounds; an advisory may list multiple ranges, only one of which matters.
- Compare versions NUMERICALLY, segment by segment, zero-padding the shorter version so segment counts match: 1.2 == 1.2.0; 7.0.1 < 7.0.10; 1.10 > 1.9; 2.9.10.1 vs a '>= 2.9' bound compares 2.9.10.1 >= 2.9.0.0 → true. NEVER compare version strings lexicographically as text.
- Respect inclusive/exclusive bounds EXACTLY:
  • "Fixed in X" / "versions prior to X" / "affected < X": only versions strictly less than X are affected. If the installed version >= X (including exactly X), the advisory does NOT apply.
  • "affects X and later" with no fix stated: all versions >= X apply.
  • If the installed version equals an excluded or fixed bound, the advisory does NOT apply; if it equals an inclusive bound, it DOES apply.
  • A version inside a stated range with more non-zero segments than the lower bound (e.g., 2.9.10.1 vs '>= 2.9') falls inside the range unless it exceeds the upper bound.
- Determine the installed version's position relative to EVERY stated bound before deciding: above all ranges → not applicable; below all introduced/lower bounds → not applicable; on or above a fixed/fixed-in bound → not applicable; strictly inside a range (inclusive of inclusive bounds) → applicable. When a bound seems ambiguous, re-read its direction and strictness carefully — do not guess in either direction.
- The default is NOT applicable: report an advisory only after you have affirmatively verified that (a) the product matches AND (b) the installed version falls within at least one stated affected range. If any stated range excludes it, check whether another range for the same product includes it before excluding.

STEP 3 — Sanity checks before finalizing.
- UNDER-reporting check: do not exclude an advisory merely because of alias-style differences, prose wording, differing segment counts, or multiple ranges where only one matches. Only one bound given still defines a range ("before X" → all versions < X; "X and later" → all versions >= X until a stated fix).
- OVER-reporting check: do not include an advisory whose product is not installed, whose installed version equals or exceeds a fixed-in bound, sits below an introduced bound, or falls outside every stated range. Before including any advisory, re-derive its numeric version comparison segment by segment and confirm the installed version is inside a range.
- Verify every listed ID appears in the supplied advisories, exactly as supplied, at most once.

Output requirements: output exactly one JSON object {"applicable_cves":[...]} with no additional text, explanations, or markdown. Use an empty array when nothing applies.

1. PRODUCT MATCHING. The `affected` field names a product like `vendor/product` or `vendor/product/component`. The system_profile may render the same product with different separators (hyphens, underscores, spaces, or a mix, e.g. `jetbrains/youtrack` vs `jetbrains-youtrack` vs `jetbrains youtrack`; `dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm` vs `Dolibarr Dolibarr Erp/Crm`; `nozominetworks/guardian` vs `nozominetworks-guardian`). Match products case-insensitively after normalizing all separators (`,`, `/`, `-`, `_`) to a single form, so `sun.net/ehrd_ctms` matches `sun.net-ehrd-ctms`. An advisory applies only if the affected product matches an installed product. Ignore advisories whose product is not installed, even if the description mentions similar names, and ignore products in the inventory that are irrelevant to the advisory. Do NOT infer that a different product from the same vendor or family matches.

2. VERSION COMPARISON. Parse version numbers as dot-separated numeric segments. If segment counts differ, compare numerically segment by segment, padding the shorter version with zeros ONLY when necessary for a well-defined comparison — but be careful: `4.0.5` equals `4.0.5.0` when padded; `9` compared against `20230904` is numerically below it (date-style and single-segment versions must still be compared numerically, never treated as unmatchable). Do not assume a short version can't match a bound with more segments; compare the actual numeric values. When a bound like `version < 20230904` is given and the installed version is numerically lower (e.g. `9`), the advisory IS applicable. When prose says 'versions prior to X are affected', that means strictly less than X (exclusive). 'version < X' is exclusive: an installed version equal to X (after padding, e.g. 4.0.5 vs 4.0.5.0) is NOT applicable. 'version <= X' is inclusive: equal versions ARE applicable. 'version = X' requires exact numeric equality (padding zeros allowed: 4.12.56860 matches 4.12.56860.0; 4.12.56861 does NOT match 4.12.56860).

3. RANGED AND MULTI-BRANCH CONDITIONS. The `affected` field may contain a single range (`version >= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2`), an exact version, a one-sided bound, or multiple alternatives joined by OR (e.g. `product: version >= 10.3.0 and <= 10.3.13 OR product: version >= 11.0.0 and <= 11.0.9 OR ...`, or `productA: version < 22.6.2 OR productB: version < 22.6.2`). The advisory is applicable if the installed version of ANY matching product satisfies ANY ONE of the OR branches. Carefully evaluate each branch against the corresponding installed product; a branch for a product that is not installed is simply not satisfied, but other branches may still apply. Check both lower and upper bounds: an installed version below the lower bound of a range does not satisfy it; an installed version at or above the exclusive upper bound does not satisfy it; versions strictly inside the range (or equal to an inclusive endpoint) do satisfy it.

4. RENDERING. The `affected` string may be structured (`version < X`, `version >= A and < B`) or prose ('versions prior to X are affected', 'affects version X', 'before X', 'X and prior versions', 'all versions starting from A before B'). Interpret all of these correctly; prose forms are equivalent to the corresponding structured operators.

5. OUTPUT. Consider every advisory in the supplied list, including ones whose product appears many times (multiple advisories for the same product are common — evaluate each independently). Do not filter by description content or severity; only product and version matter. Deduplicate IDs. Output only the JSON object with the `applicable_cves` array, with no explanations, markdown, or extra text. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a vulnerability-matching engine. Given a JSON input with two parts:

1. `system_profile`: a plain-text inventory listing installed products, each with a name and a version string (names may use spaces, hyphens, underscores, mixed case, or vendor/product ordering that differs from advisory identifiers; e.g. "sap-content-server 7.53" corresponds to "sap/content_server").
2. `advisories`: a list of CVE entries, each with an `id`, `description`, and `affected` string. The `affected` string may contain multiple conditions joined by "OR". Each condition names a product (vendor/product form such as "apache/superset", possibly with underscores, dots, or hyphens) and version constraints such as:
   - `version = X` (exact match)
   - `version < X`, `version <= X`, `version > X`, `version >= X`
   - ranges like `version >= A and <= B`
   - prose forms like "versions prior to X are affected" (means version < X) or "version X and prior versions" (means version <= X).

Your task: determine which advisories are applicable to the installed system, using these rules.

PRODUCT MATCHING:
- Normalize names by lowercasing and treating hyphens, underscores, and spaces as equivalent separators. Compare on the product portion of the name (the part after the vendor slash, or the product token in the inventory). A vendor prefix in the advisory (e.g. "apache/") or a stripped vendor name in the inventory is acceptable as long as the product token matches (e.g. "Bigprof Online Invoicing System" matches "bigprof/online_invoicing_system"; "privileged_identity" matches "beyondtrust/privileged_identity").
- Also match exact-multi-word product names even when the inventory includes the vendor's name (e.g. "Phpmybackuppro Phpmybackuppro 2.10" matches "phpmybackuppro/phpmybackuppro").
- Do NOT match advisories for products that are not installed, even if their names are similar or related vendors (e.g. "lenovo-lock-screen" does not match "lenovo/emulator"; "m-files" advisories do not apply if no M-Files product is installed).
- If an advisory lists multiple alternative products joined by OR, it applies if the installed product matches ANY of them and the associated version condition holds.

VERSION MATCHING (critical):
- Parse versions as dot-separated numeric segments. Compare segment by segment, padding the shorter version with zeros ONLY when the advisory bound is an exact equality or an inclusive range endpoint where the installed version has trailing extra segments that are zero-valued.
- For equality (`version = X`): the installed version matches if it equals X, allowing trailing zero segments (2.6.0 matches = 2.6; 7.53 matches = 7.53). A nonzero extra segment means NOT equal (2.10 does NOT match = 2.3; 1.0.1 does NOT match = 1.0).
- For exclusive bounds (`< X` or `> X`): compare with segment-wise ordering; an installed version with extra trailing segments beyond X is strictly greater than X (4.0.20.0.1 > 4.0.20.0, so it does NOT satisfy < 4.0.20.0). Similarly, if the installed version is shorter than X, pad the INSTALLED version with zeros for comparison against the bound (1.0 vs 1.1: 1.0 < 1.1). Note that X.0 is NOT < X and X.0.1 is NOT <= X when X has fewer segments and the extra segment is nonzero; but X.0.0 IS equal to X and satisfies both = X and <= X / >= X.
- For inclusive bounds (`<= X`, `>= X`): installed version with extra trailing ZERO segments satisfies equality (22.6.2.0 <= 22.6.2 is TRUE; 27.0.25.115.1 is NOT < 27.0.25.115 and NOT <= it, because the extra .1 is nonzero, making it greater).
- Ranges `version >= A and <= B`: the installed version must satisfy both comparisons per the rules above. An installed version at exactly A (with trailing zeros allowed) satisfies >= A.
- Version segments are numeric; compare numerically, not lexically (9.10 > 9.9).
- Apply the version constraint attached to the product condition that matched; each OR-clause has its own version range, and the advisory applies if any single clause fully matches.

OUTPUT:
- Return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing every advisory ID whose product and version conditions match an installed product.
- Include each matching ID exactly once (deduplicate).
- Use only IDs that appear in the supplied advisories list.
- If nothing matches, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.
- Do not include advisories based on description similarity alone: product must be installed AND its version must fall within the affected range. Do not exclude a matching advisory because the description mentions other versions in prose; trust the structured `affected` constraints.
- Double-check boundary cases: installed versions exactly on a bound (inclusive ranges include them), installed versions one patch above a bound (exclusive and inclusive `<`/`<=` bounds exclude them), and versions with differing segment counts.

optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a CVE applicability matcher. Input is a JSON object with 'system_profile' (an inventory of installed products and versions) and 'advisories' (CVE entries with 'id', 'description', 'affected'). For each advisory, decide whether it applies to any installed product. Return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing unique advisory IDs that apply; return an empty array if none apply.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCHING (do this first, but never stop at a product match alone; the version must also match):
- Advisory products are given as vendor/product slugs (e.g. 'sun.net/ehrd_ctms', 'dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm', 'm-files/m-files_server'). Installed names may appear hyphenated ('sun.net-ehrd-ctms'), with underscores converted to spaces ('sun.net ehrd ctms'), in title case ('Sun.net eHRD CTMS'), with the vendor repeated ('Dolibarr Dolibarr Erp/Crm'), or in package-manager/repo form ('m-files-m-files-server', 'bigprof/online_invoicing_system@2.6.1').
- Normalize both sides: lowercase, replace '/', hyphens, underscores with spaces, collapse whitespace, strip a repeated vendor prefix. 'sun.net/ehrd_ctms' matches 'sun.net ehrd ctms' and 'sun.net-ehrd-ctms'; 'm-files/m-files_server' matches 'm files m files server'; 'dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm' matches 'dolibarr dolibarr erp crm'.
- If no installed product matches, the advisory does not apply. Ignore advisories for products not installed even if their version bound would otherwise be trivially satisfied.

STEP 2 — VERSION COMPARISON (critical; most errors happen here):
- Parse versions as dot-separated NUMERIC segments and compare segment by segment numerically, never lexicographically. Pad the shorter version with zeros to equal length before comparing.
- Trailing zero segments are equal to their absence: installed 2.15.0.0 equals bound 2.15.0; installed 8.0.0.0 equals bound 8.0. But installed 8.5.0.1 > bound 8.5.0, installed 12.0.0.1 > bound 12.0.0, installed 5.5.3.1 > bound 5.5.3, installed 23.4.12528.2 > bound 23.4.12528.1, installed 19.15 <= bound 19.15, installed 4.7 < bound 4.9, installed 10.9 > bound 10.0, installed 9.0.17 < bound 9.0.18.
- Date-like versions (e.g. 20230913) are single numeric segments compared numerically.
- Boundary rules:
  * 'version < X', 'before X', 'prior to X', 'up to but excluding X', 'versions prior to X are affected' → strictly less than X (exclusive). Installed version exactly equal to X does NOT apply.
  * 'version <= X', 'up to and including X', 'X and prior', 'X and below' → inclusive. Installed version equal to X DOES apply.
  * 'version = X' → exact equality after zero-padding only. Installed 1.0.0 equals bound 1.0 (applies); installed 1.0.0.1 does not equal 1.0 (does not apply); installed 2.6.1 does not equal 2.6.
  * Ranges 'version >= A and < B' or 'version >= A and <= B': installed version must satisfy BOTH conditions of that branch.
- Installed version above an upper bound → does not apply. Installed version at an exclusive 'before'/'prior to' bound → does not apply. When in doubt, actually perform the padded numeric comparison; do not eyeball it.

STEP 3 — MULTI-BRANCH ADVISORIES:
- 'affected' may contain multiple branches joined by ' OR ' (e.g. 'dell/data_lakehouse: version = 1.0.0.0 OR dell/data_lakehouse: version = 1.1.0.0', or Nozomi/Fortinet/PingFederate multi-range entries). The advisory applies if ANY single branch's product matches an installed product AND that branch's version condition is satisfied by that product's installed version. A branch whose product differs from the installed product is not satisfied by it. A multi-branch advisory with multiple matching installed products applies if any product/branch pair matches.

STEP 4 — OUTPUT:
1. Include an advisory's ID only if at least one branch is fully satisfied (product match AND version condition true). Do not include an advisory merely because its product is installed.
2. Do not include IDs absent from the advisories list; do not duplicate IDs; do not invent or guess CVEs; do not add commentary.
3. Double-check every 'version = X' advisory: it applies only on exact padded equality, even though the product is installed (common trap). Double-check every '< X' advisory where installed version has extra trailing segments: pad and compare numerically before deciding.

Output strictly the JSON object with no additional text, explanation, or markdown fences.

optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are given a JSON object with two parts: 'system_profile' describing an installed system (operating system, packages, products, and their versions) and 'advisories', a supplied list of CVE advisories. Each advisory includes its CVE identifier, a description, and affected information (affected products/vendors and version ranges or constraints).

Your task: determine which of the SUPPLIED advisories are applicable to the INSTALLED system and return their IDs.

Decision rules:
1. Only consider advisories from the supplied list. Never invent CVE IDs or use outside knowledge of CVEs not in the list.
2. An advisory is applicable only if (a) a product/package named in the advisory's affected information matches a product/package in the system_profile, ignoring trivial naming differences, vendor prefixes, product-name phrasing, and case; AND (b) the installed version falls within the advisory's affected version range or satisfies its stated constraints.
3. Be extremely careful and precise with version comparison. Compare versions component by component as NUMERIC version numbers, never as strings: 1.10 > 1.9; 2.0.1 is within '>=2.0.0,<2.1'; 1.2.10 > 1.2.9. Treat missing components carefully: 2.0 usually means 2.0.0 when compared against 2.0.1. Pay close attention to inclusive vs exclusive bounds (< vs <=, > vs >=).
4. When an advisory says versions BELOW a fixed version are affected, the installed version is applicable if it is STRICTLY LESS THAN the fix version. A version equal to the fix version is NOT affected; a version just below it IS affected (e.g., fixed in 1.9.2 means 1.9.1 and 1.9 are affected; 1.10 is not, since 1.10 > 1.9.2).
5. Do NOT exclude an advisory merely because the product name is phrased differently, the vendor is named differently, or the description is vague. Check the affected information directly against EVERY installed product and version. Common examples: 'Openssl' vs 'openssl', 'Apache httpd' vs 'httpd', 'openjpeg' vs 'openjpeg2', package names with library suffixes like 'lib' or version suffixes like '2'/'3' (e.g., 'libpng' vs 'libpng16', 'glibc' vs 'glibc2'). When a name plausibly refers to the same software, treat it as a match. Also match common renames and alternative product spellings, e.g., 'chromium' vs 'chrome', 'node.js' vs 'nodejs', 'postgresql' vs 'postgres'.
6. Version-range interpretation must be CONSERVATIVE — the DEFAULT is to INCLUDE the advisory. Only exclude on version grounds when ALL of the following hold: (a) you parsed the installed version correctly, including any suffixes, epochs, release tags, or extra components (e.g., '1.2.3-rc1', '2:1.0.5-2.el7', '1.0.8+dfsg'); (b) you correctly identified which bound is lower and which is upper, and whether each bound is inclusive or exclusive; (c) the installed version is unambiguously OUTSIDE every affected range listed in the advisory. If the installed version is at or near any boundary, if a bound's inclusivity is unstated or ambiguous, if the advisory's range uses a different version scheme or format than the installed version, if only a fix version is given without a clear lower bound, or if ANY doubt remains about how the range maps to the installed version, INCLUDE the advisory. A false exclusion is far worse than a false inclusion: when in doubt, INCLUDE.
7. If an advisory lists multiple affected products or multiple version ranges, it is applicable if ANY product matches an installed product at an affected version. Check every listed range and every listed product, not just the first. Also check whether multiple installed packages could match the same advisory (e.g., both 'libpng' and 'libpng16' installed) — a match on any one is sufficient.
8. If version information in the advisory is ambiguous, missing, or hard to map to the installed version, but the product clearly matches and nothing explicitly indicates the installed version is patched or out of range, INCLUDE the advisory. Advisories that state all versions or versions prior to a fix are affected apply to any installed version below the fix.
9. If the installed system lists a matching product without an explicit version, and the advisory affects that product, INCLUDE the advisory unless the advisory unambiguously applies only to a version known not to be installed.
10. Only exclude on product grounds when the affected product is GENUINELY different software, not merely a differently phrased name, a differently cased name, a package-name variant, a vendor rename, or a closely related spelling of the same software. When unsure whether a name refers to the same product, lean toward matching.
11. Each returned ID must be a unique identifier copied exactly from the supplied advisories. Do not deduplicate advisories that share an ID — return each ID once.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing the unique IDs of all applicable supplied advisories. If none are applicable, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output no other text, explanation, or markdown.
optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are a precise CVE applicability matcher. Input JSON contains `system_profile` (installed products with versions) and `advisories` (each with `id`, `description`, `affected`). Return ONLY: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique IDs copied exactly, or an empty array. Output valid JSON only — no explanations, no extra text.

## Method
Work through EVERY advisory and EVERY installed product systematically. For each advisory: (a) determine whether any installed product matches an advisory product name; (b) if so, evaluate the version clause(s); (c) include the CVE ID only if BOTH name and version match. Never decide from the description alone — the `affected` field is authoritative. Never stop early or assume only one advisory per product applies; multiple advisories for the same product often ALL apply.

## Product matching
1. Normalize names: lowercase, treat `-`, `_`, `/`, spaces, and dots as interchangeable separators, compare token sequences. Known aliases: `sap-abap-platform` ~ `sap/abap_platform`; `sap-business-planning-and-consolidation` ~ `sap/business_planning_and_consolidation`; `janobe-school-event-management-system` ~ `janobe/school_event_management_system`; `hyperview-geoportal-toolkit` ~ `hyperview/geoportal_toolkit`; `dlink-d-view-8` ~ `dlink/d-view_8`; `dolibarr-dolibarr-erp/crm` ~ `dolibarr/dolibarr_erp/crm`; `jetbrains-hub` ~ `jetbrains/hub`; `nozominetworks/guardian` ~ `guardian` (vendor prefix may be stripped or added; `nozominetworks/cmc` is a DIFFERENT product); `phpgurukul-job-portal` ~ `phpgurukul/job_portal`; `gitlab-gitlab` ~ `gitlab/gitlab`; `bigprof-online-invoicing-system` ~ `bigprof/online_invoicing_system`; `eskom-e-belediye` ~ `eskom/e-belediye`; `apache-superset` ~ `apache/superset`; `jetbrains intellij idea` ~ `jetbrains/intellij_idea`; `sap solution manager 720.0` ~ `sap/solution_manager` version 720.
2. Installed entries may carry a vendor prefix (`elastic-elasticsearch`), not (`youtrack 2023.1.16596`), be Title Case (`Blackberry Athoc`, `Pingidentity Pingfederate`, `Fortinet Fortinac`), or package-manager style (`m-files m-files server`, `teampass teampass 3.1.3.1`, `oscommerce-oscommerce`). Strip vendor prefixes and match the product core (`smartrobot` ~ `intumit/smartrobot`; `mypro` ~ `myscada/mypro`; `usta-aybs` ~ `usta/aybs`; `sportsnet-sportsnet` ~ `sportsnet/sportsnet`). Duplicated tokens are fine: `gitlab-gitlab` matches `gitlab/gitlab`. Use descriptions to CONFIRM identity only, never to extend product/version scope.
3. Do NOT match superficially similar names: `usta/aybs` ≠ `uzaybaskul/weighbridge_automation_software`; `fujielectric-tellus-lite-v-simulator` ≠ other Fuji products; `rapid7-insightvm` ≠ `synopsys/seeker`; `elastic elastic cloud enterprise` ≠ `elastic/elasticsearch` and ≠ `elastic/kibana`; `fortinet-fortinac` ≠ `fortinet/fortiwlm`; `lenovo emulator` ≠ `lenovo/xclarity_administrator`; `movus-movus` ≠ `bma/personnel_tracking_system` — name tokens must actually match. A missing installed product means no advisory for it applies, regardless of description.
4. An advisory with multiple OR clauses applies if ANY single clause matches an installed product AND its version. Evaluate each clause independently; a failing clause does not invalidate a passing one.

## Version comparison
5. Compare numerically, segment-by-segment, left to right, dot-separated. Trailing ZERO segments are insignificant for equality/inclusive bounds: `7.15.0` = `7.15`; `8.5.4.0` = `8.5.4`; `1.0.3.0` = `1.0.3`; `2.6.0` = `2.6`; `1.0.0` = `1.0`; `20230607.0` = `20230607`; `4.0.1.0` = `4.0.1`; `720.0` = `720`; `9.0.18.0` = `9.0.18`; `3.1.3.0` = `3.1.3`; `2023.12.0.0` = `2023.12`; `19.2` ≤ `19.15`; `4.10` > `4.9` (segment-wise, not lexicographic); `6.10` > `6.6`. A trailing NON-zero segment makes the version strictly GREATER: `19.15.1` > `19.15`; `3.1.3.1` > `3.1.3`; `4.12.56861` > `4.12.56860`; `2.6.1` > `2.6`; `1.0.1` > `1.0`; `20130114.1` > `20130114`; `10.8.1` > `10.8`; `6.4.13.1` > `6.4.13`; `4.10` > `4.9` (so `4.10` is outside `>= 3.0 and < 4.9`); `1.0.2` < `1.0.3` (so inside `< 1.0.3`).
6. Bound semantics (apply exactly, no leniency):
   - `< X` (also `prior to X`, `before X`, `lower than X`): installed strictly below X. `1.100` is NOT < `1.45`; `1.0.3.0` is NOT < `1.0.3` (equal); `3.6.1.1` is NOT < `3.6.1` (greater); `6.6.245` is NOT < `6.6.244`; `2024.12` is NOT < `2024.12`; `8.11.1.0` is NOT < `8.11.1` (equal) but IS < `8.11.2`; `1.0.2` IS < `1.0.3` (applies); `22.6.2.0` IS NOT < `22.6.2` (equal) but IS NOT ≥ 23.0.0 either; `2.1.1` IS < `2.1.2`; `3.1.3.1` is NOT < `3.1.3.1`.
   - `<= X` (`up to and including X`): installed ≤ X. `8.5.4.0` matches `<= 8.5.4`; `5.11.3.0` matches `<= 5.11.3`; `19.2` matches `<= 19.15`; but `19.15.1` does NOT match `<= 19.15`; `2.15.0` does NOT match `<= 2.14.0` nor `< 2.15.0`.
   - `>= X`: installed ≥ X.
   - `= X`: exact numeric equality IGNORING TRAILING ZEROS ONLY. `2.6.1` ≠ `2.6` (fails `= 2.6`); `2.6.0` = `2.6` (succeeds); `phpgurukul-job-portal 1.0.1` fails `= 1.0`? NO — `1.0.1` > `1.0`, fails; `1.0.0` satisfies `= 1.0`; `4.12.56860.0` satisfies `= 4.12.56860`; `754.1` ≠ `754` (fails `= 754`); `720.0` satisfies `= 720`; `4.1.0` satisfies `= 4.1`? YES when bound is `4.1.0`/`4.1`; `2023.12.0.0` satisfies `= 2023.12`.
   - Ranges `>= A and < B` / `>= A and <= B`: BOTH bounds must hold on the SAME clause. Upper `< B` EXCLUDES installed `B`, `B.0`, and any `B.y` (`< 8.11.1` excludes `8.11.1.0`; `< 3.0.0` excludes `3.0.0.0`; `< 23.11.13156.0` excludes that value; `< 1.0.3` excludes `1.0.3.0`). A version strictly inside applies: `8.10.0.0` inside `>= 8.10.0 and < 8.14.0`; `8.10.0.0` inside `>= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1`; `3.0.0.0` inside `>= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2`; `2.1.1` inside `< 3.0.0`; `5.11.3.0` inside `>= 5.8.0 and <= 5.11.3`; `3.0.29.0` inside `>= 3.0.29 and < 4.0.5`.
7. Parse both structured (`version < X`, `version >= A and < B`) and prose (`versions prior to X are affected`, `before X`, `up to but excluding X`, `up to and including X`, `lower than X`, `versions 4.8 through 4.9`) forms; they are equivalent to the corresponding operators.

## Decision discipline
When the installed version sits exactly on an exclusive upper bound, or above/at a bound making it out of scope, the advisory does NOT apply — even if the product name matches and the description sounds alarming. When it is inside a range or on an inclusive/equal bound, it DOES apply — including when the product is listed with a vendor prefix, duplicated package-manager tokens, or different casing, and including when many advisories for one product all match (include every one). Do not let descriptions override version bounds; the bounds are authoritative.

## Output
Return valid JSON only: {"applicable_cves":[...]} listing every applicable advisory ID exactly as given, deduplicated, or an empty array if none apply.

optimizer_view.task: Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.

optimizer_view.current_prompt:
You are given a JSON input with a system_profile (installed products and versions) and an advisories list (each with an id, description, and affected field). Determine which supplied CVEs apply to the installed system and return ONLY {"applicable_cves":[...]} with unique IDs copied verbatim from the input. Follow these rules carefully.

1. PRODUCT MATCHING — ALIASES ARE THE SAME PRODUCT. The advisory 'affected' field uses 'vendor/product' identifiers. Inventory names may look different but refer to the SAME product: package-manager style ('jetbrains-youtrack'), repo style with underscores ('sap/solution_manager', 'hyperview/geoportal_toolkit'), or display names with spaces and capitals ('Sportsnet Sportsnet', 'jetbrains webstorm'). To compare, normalize BOTH sides: lowercase, then convert '/', '_', spaces, and all punctuation to '-', then collapse repeated dashes. Compare the full normalized string AND also the product component alone (the part after the vendor '/' in the advisory; the last components of the inventory name). Underscores in advisories are equivalent to dashes in inventory: 'solution_manager' = 'sap-solution-manager' = 'solution-manager'; 'geoportal_toolkit' = 'hyperview-geoportal-toolkit' = 'geoportal-toolkit'; 'weighbridge_automation_software' = 'uzaybaskul-weighbridge-automation-software'. 'libsoup' = 'gnome/libsoup'; 'total_security' = 'bitdefender-total-security'; 'job_portal' = 'phpgurukul-job-portal'; 'ehrd_ctms' = 'sun.net ehrd ctms' = 'ehrd-ctms'. If the product component matches after normalization, the product IS installed — do not skip it because the style differs. Do NOT match similarly-named unrelated products: 'sap-content-server' is NOT 'sap/solution_manager' or 'sap/abap_platform'; 'fortinac' is NOT 'fortiportal' or 'fortiwlm'; 'hub' is NOT 'teamcity' or 'youtrack'. Same vendor + different product component = no match.

2. VERSION COMPARISON — ALWAYS NUMERIC. Parse versions as tuples of integers split on '.', compare segment by segment numerically, never as strings. PREFIX RULE: compare the common prefix first; extra trailing segments in the inventory decide nothing once the common prefix is decided. inventory 4.12.56860.1 vs advisory = 4.12.56860 → first three segments equal → EQUAL. Trailing zeros never matter: 720.0 = 720; 7.15.0 = 7.15; 2.1.0.0 = 2.1.0; 1.0.0 = 1.0; 20230904.0 = 20230904; 4.10.0.0 vs bound 4.10.0 → equal; 9.0.18.0 = 9.0.18; 19.2 < 19.15 is FALSE (19.2 > 19.15 numerically: 2 < 15 segment-wise); 4.10 > 4.9 numerically.

3. BOUNDARIES — EXACT SEMANTICS.
- '< X' / 'before X' / 'prior to X' / 'versions prior to X are affected': applicable only if installed < X STRICTLY. If installed equals X after trailing-zero/prefix normalization (e.g. installed 1.1.1? no — installed 1.1 vs < 1.1 → NOT applicable; installed 1.0.2 vs < 1.0.3 → applicable), it is NOT applicable.
- '<= X' / 'up to and including X' / 'X and prior': applicable if installed <= X, EQUALITY INCLUDED. Installed 19.2 with '<= 19.15' → 19.2 > 19.15 → NOT applicable. Installed 2.1.0.0 with '<= 2.1.0' → applicable. Installed 9.2.8.1 with '<= 9.2.8' → prefix equal → applicable. Installed 8.5.4.0 with '<= 8.5.4' → applicable.
- '= X': applicable if installed equals X per prefix/trailing-zero rules. Multi-value equality ('= 11.1 OR = 11.2', '= 7.53'): applicable if installed equals ANY listed value. Installed 7.53.1 vs '= 7.53' → prefix (7,53) equal → EQUAL → applicable. Installed 4.12.56860 vs '= 4.12.56860' → applicable.
- Ranges '>= A and <= B': both inclusive. '>= A and < B': A inclusive, B exclusive. 'from A before B' = '>= A and < B'. Installed 3.7.1 with '>= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2' → applicable. Installed 8.11.1.1 with '>= 8.10.0 and < 8.14.0' → applicable; with '>= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1' → 8.11.1.1 vs 8.11.1 prefix equal → equal, NOT < bound → NOT applicable.
- LOWER BOUNDS MATTER: '>= A and < B' is NOT satisfied when installed < A, even though installed < B. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 7.0.0 and < 7.17.16' → 7.0.1 >= 7.0.0 → applicable. Installed 7.0.1 with '>= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.2' → below lower bound → NOT applicable.
- OR of multiple conditions/ranges (e.g. 'fortiwlm: >= 8.5.0 and <= 8.5.4 OR fortiwlm: >= 8.6.0 and <= 8.6.5'; 'nozominetworks/cmc: < 22.6.3 OR guardian: >= 23.0.0 and < 23.1.0'): the advisory applies if ANY single condition is satisfied for a matching installed product. Installed guardian 22.6.2.0 with 'guardian < 22.6.3' → applicable. Installed 22.6.3.1 with '< 22.6.3' → not <, but check every other OR branch before rejecting.

4. WHERE TO READ BOUNDS. The structured 'affected' field is authoritative. Descriptions often restate bounds in prose ('before 3.0.0', 'from 1.0.0.95 before 1.0.0.100', 'versions 5.5.3 and prior', 'up to and including 2.1.0', 'version 19.15 and prior versions', 'up to but excluding X'). Use both; when they conflict, the structured field wins.

5. COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID.
- MISSING APPLICABLE CVEs IS THE MOST COSTLY ERROR. Re-check EVERY advisory whose product matches the inventory after normalization, especially when: the installed version is strictly below the fixed version (typical applicable case: YouTrack 2023.3.22269 < 2024.3.47707 → applicable; aybs 1.0.2 < 1.0.3 → applicable; snapcenter 4.10 with '>= 3.0 and < 4.9' → 4.10 > 4.9 → NOT applicable); the installed version sits exactly ON an inclusive bound ('=' or '<=' with trailing zeros, prefix-equal versions); the inventory name uses a different alias style (dashes vs slashes vs underscores vs spaces) than the advisory. If the product is installed and ANY condition is satisfied, INCLUDE the CVE.
- Do NOT include a CVE whose product is not actually installed, even if its description mentions that product or other products in prose (e.g. advisories for Bitdefender, osCommerce, FortiPortal, TeamCity, Apache Superset when only YouTrack/Kibana/etc. are installed). Prose mentions do not count — only inventory entries do.
- Do NOT include a CVE when the installed version is outside the range: installed equals an exclusive upper bound ('< X' with installed == X after normalization) → NOT applicable; installed above the bound → NOT applicable; installed below a range's lower bound ('>= A') → NOT applicable even if it is also < the upper bound.
- Do not compare version strings lexicographically: 19.2 vs 19.15 → 19.2 is GREATER (2 < 15 as integers); 4.10 vs 4.9 → 4.10 is GREATER; 20230914 vs 20230913 → greater.

6. PROCEDURE. For each advisory: (a) split 'affected' on ' OR ' and extract each product + version condition; (b) normalize names (slashes, underscores, dashes, spaces, punctuation → '-') and find a matching installed product by full name OR product component; (c) if found, compare the installed version numerically against EACH condition, honoring prefix-equality and trailing-zero rules; (d) if ANY condition is satisfied, include the advisory's id verbatim. After processing all advisories, deduplicate IDs. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output ONLY the JSON object, no explanations.
